use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The C2 JU resolves dual designations by periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks and, upon recognizing two tracks eligible for correlation, transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message to request correlation and identify the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU resolves dual designations by periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks and, upon recognizing two tracks eligible for correlation, transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message to request correlation and identify the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has a capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
The C2 JU performs correlation and decorrelation of its local track data with respect to the remote data which it is receiving.
The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
The dual designation to be resolved is an air or surface track dual designation.
Two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability.

When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

trigger.raw_text: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

claims.content: The C2 JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.

The two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions twice before the correlation is executed; when the two tracks pass once, they are deemed a tentative correlation, the same two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus, and if they successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they are processed for dual designation resolution.
The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

The C2 JU selects the higher TN as the TN to be dropped in the absence of a selection constraint, and shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7).
The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

The originating JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, using the Response Value (RV) field; RV value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable and RV value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.

The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate, i.e., when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate, the correlation shall be rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint. If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection (see paragraph 4.7.3.2.c).

Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.

Confirm the restriction, thereby inhibiting the correlation, or conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation; if the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.

If certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow a receiving IU to reject the requested correlation, the receiving IU rejects the requested correlation; exit with the correlation request rejected.

If certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow a receiving IU to respond with a reverse correlation request, the receiving IU responds with a reverse correlation request; exit with a reverse correlation request originated.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation and the RV field is set to value 0, a reverse correlation request shall be originated; exit with a reverse correlation request originated.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation and the RV field is set to value 1, the original correlation request shall be rejected; exit with the original correlation request rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection; exit with the rejection reported.

When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection (see paragraph 4.7.3.2.c); if such conditions apply, the correlation shall be rejected; exit with the correlation rejected.
The dual designation is resolved.
The correlation of the two tracks is executed.
The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation.
The C2 JU ceases reporting the track and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
Each tracked object is reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports.

In the absence of a selection constraint, the higher TN is selected as the TN to be dropped, and a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7) is not automatically selected as the TN to be dropped.
If the ID conflict is resolved, the TN to be retained is tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test is conducted only once.
